chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkill (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated to us, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Qatadah al-Qummi, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Yahya narrated to us, on the authority of Aban al-Ahmar, from Al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both)

He said: 'And by the One who sent my grandfather (peace be upon him and his family) as a righteous prophet, verily Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, provides sustenance to a servant according to his generosity. And verily, help descends from Heaven according to the extent of the need. And verily, patience descends according to the severity of the affliction.'

key_terms.الْمَعُونَةُ: Help, aid, or assistance from Heaven.
key_terms.الْمُؤُونَةُ: The need, consumption, or extent of requirement for which help is needed.
key_terms.الْمُرُوَّةُ: Generosity, manliness, or virtue; specifically referring to the capacity or generosity of the servant.
key_terms.جَدِّي: My grandfather (referring to Prophet Muhammad SAWW).

ai.seo_question: How is divine provision related to human generosity in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the divine principle of proportional reciprocity, linking spiritual virtues to their corresponding divine rewards. This teaching underscores the Shia understanding that God’s generosity is not arbitrary but calibrated to the servant's capacity for giving and enduring, reinforcing the concept that trials are measured to foster spiritual growth.
